answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
**Running again:** Expect three days with no running, then a short, easy 2 miles on Thu Oct 22. Do it only if the stairs feel normal, a 20-minute walk is pain-free and the blister is covered. If not, wait until Sat Oct 24, because a few extra days cost you nothing. After that, plan on easy running only through Nov 1.

**The Thanksgiving 10K:** Don't commit yet. Five weeks is enough time to run it, but after two easy weeks you'd have about three weeks of real 10K preparation. You also haven't run faster than marathon pace since the Sep 23 threshold session. Treat it as a fun race, not one to chase a time in, and decide after next week's runs.

**What comes next:** In your next check-in, tell me which pulls you most: the 10K, another marathon with a faster target, or a few relaxed weeks with no goal. Your answer decides the next block.

new.analysis:
The race did what the build was meant to do, and now it needs a proper recovery before anything else. Everything planned for the week was done, including the Wednesday marathon-pace session and the full 26.2 miles on Sunday. You missed 3:45 by about five minutes and beat your first marathon by 12.

You paced the first 20 miles well. The front half averaged 8:32/mi, a touch quicker than the 8:35/mi that 3:45 needs, and the back half slowed to 8:58/mi, with the last 10K near 9:28/mi. A late fade is common in a second marathon, and the course climbed 617 ft, more than any of your long runs. That is worth a look when you plan the next marathon, not now.

The overload note in your weekly report is the race itself. A relative effort of 472 and 2 h 26 min in the hard zones are one marathon, and the low easy-running share is normal for a race week. Neither changes the plan.

Next week is light because the damage is in the muscles, not your aerobic fitness. Quads that struggle on stairs are still repairing, and running on them adds stress without adding fitness. Your sleep also dropped to 6.5 hours on average, which slows that repair.

The week of Oct 26 – Nov 1 should stay easy too, at roughly 12 to 15 miles with no faster running. Two easy weeks gives your legs time to recover fully. It also gives you time to choose a direction before I build anything new.

safetyCallouts.title: Blister and soreness.
safetyCallouts.body: Keep the blister clean and covered, and see a doctor if it turns red, hot, swollen or starts to ooze. Soreness should ease each day. If pain turns sharp, stays in one spot, gets worse or one calf swells, stop running and see a physio or doctor.
